A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe the same ResVLA work and contain matching main sections, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. The text and visual material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResVLA simulation results, training and inference efficiency experiments in Figure 3, and ALOHA robot experiments in Table 5. Appendix Table 6 provides detailed robustness results.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original ResVLA simulation results in Tables 1-4 and 6, while retaining the efficiency experiments and real-robot results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same spectral intent anchor, condition-dependent source, residual flow matching, training objective, and inference procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both use the same four LIBERO suites, seven LIBERO-Plus perturbation axes, Google Robot and WidowX tasks in SimplerEnv, and ALOHA cup-picking, handover, and placement task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and baseline scores remain unchanged within Tables 1-5. The efficiency comparison against π0 and the real-robot comparison against π0.5 are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, metrics, perturbation protocols, model configuration, and evaluation trial counts remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B-C. No setting change is stated to accompany the revised scores.

E4.justification: The same perturbation tests, per-suite robustness breakdown, dropout sensitivity comparison, NFE sweep, and qualitative robot examples are retained. Numerical outcomes change, but no analysis or test design is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Trial-count disclosures, including ten ALOHA trials, remain unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Central simulation results change substantially under unchanged reported settings. ResVLA averages change from 96.3% to 96.6% on LIBERO, 75.3% to 76.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 68.4% to 62.2% on Google Robot, and 57.9% to 68.8% on WidowX. Google Robot now trails InternVLA-M1 Vanilla, while WidowX now exceeds GR00T N1.5. Appendix Table 6 also changes throughout; Figure 3 and ALOHA results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, quantization and transport-cost propositions, loss-collapse theorem, and Appendix A proofs and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims about intent anchoring, residual refinement, robustness, and efficiency retain their meaning and scope. Changing 'competitive' to 'strong' and removing 'significantly' from one contribution bullet are wording edits; the abstract and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The semantic-alignment and path-straightening explanations remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning camera sensitivity, alternative anchors, and validation at scale. No new interpretation or qualification accompanies the revised results.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same backbone, fine-tuning description, hardware, optimizer settings, and hyperparameters. Project and code links are unchanged, and no additional reproducibility explanation accompanies the updated scores.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are identical, including the distinction between constructing condition-dependent sources and proposing a new bridge algorithm. References merely reflow across pages.

P1.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgements, replaces the preprint footer with ICML/PMLR publication information, and makes small front-matter and contribution-list edits. The scientific exposition and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: Benchmark tables update bolding and underlining to reflect changed rankings. The publication footer and acknowledgements cause modest text and reference reflow; figures, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 introduces text-table inconsistencies: Section 5.4 still quotes Google Robot and WidowX averages of 68.4% and 57.9%, whereas Tables 3-4 now report 62.2% and 68.8%. Section 5.2 likewise retains obsolete robustness scores. These discrepancies reduce reporting clarity and internal consistency. The added funding disclosure is useful, but the mixed score revisions provide no demonstrated quality gain that offsets this limited deterioration.
